title: Commander Canvas — Assurance Ledger for Staged Launches
body:
Purpose:
A compact operational ledger to drive staged launches (canary → ramp → full) with a single commander view. Designed for product ops, on-call, and launch leads to agree on go/no-go signals, owners, and immediate rollback triggers. This is intentionally lightweight — use as the canonical checklist during the live window and afterward as the source for the launch postmortem notes.

Scope:
- Applies to API product features, model rollouts, routing/policy changes, and capacity adjustments in Hosted/Dedicated clusters.
- Intended for launches where traffic is moved gradually (percent-based or cohort-based).
- Not intended for database-only migrations or long-running backend infra changes (separate runbooks exist).

How to use (quick):
1. Fill priority lanes and acceptance criteria at T-48h.
2. Populate KPI thresholds and owners.
3. During live window the commander updates observed status each cadence tick.
4. If any lane hits RED, consult contingency lattice and escalate.

Priority lanes (rows represent lanes to monitor):
- User-Facing Latency (p50/p95/p99) — Owner: Marcus Lee
- Error Rate (5xx, 4xx anomalies) — Owner: Priya Nair
- Cost per 1k tokens (unit economics) — Owner: Finance-ops (Evan)
- Model Quality Signals (regression rate on eval prompts) — Owner: Applied ML
- Capacity / Queue Depth (backpressure) — Owner: SRE
- Observability & Logging Integrity (sample coverage) — Owner: Observability

KPI definitions and acceptance thresholds (example):
- Latency p95: Green < 180ms, Amber 180–350ms, Red > 350ms
- Error rate 5xx (rolling 5m): Green < 0.2%, Amber 0.2–0.8%, Red > 0.8%
- Cost per 1k tokens (moving 24h avg): Green within +10% budget, Amber +10–30%, Red > +30%
- Model regression (eval set): Green < 1% regressions, Amber 1–3%, Red > 3%
- Queue depth: Green < 1000, Amber 1000–3000, Red > 3000

Acceptance criteria (must be unanimously OK across lanes to advance traffic step):
- Canary → ramp: No lane in Red for 30 continuous minutes and Amber lanes have mitigation plans in place.
- Ramp → open: 6 hours of stable metrics at target traffic with no new regressions and no more than one transient Amber episode.

Traffic ramp schedule (example):
- T0 (canary start): 1% traffic for 30m
- T0 + 30m: Evaluate; if green, 5% for 1h
- T0 + 1h30m: Evaluate; if green, 25% for 2h
- T0 + 3h30m: Evaluate; if green, 100%

Pre-launch - T-48h checklist (owners assigned):
- Confirm ticket list and ownership (product ops)
- Verify monitoring dashboards + synthetic probes (observability)
- Run dry-run traffic test in staging (SRE)
- Confirm rollback image/commit and routing policy (release engineering)
- Notify support & account teams; post update in #product-launch (comms)

Launch day cadence (commander ticks):
- T-15m: Final sanity checks, confirm on-call presence, declare channels
- T0: Start canary, commander marks each lane status (Green/Amber/Red)
- Every 30m during canary/ramp: Update statuses, note anomalies and actions
- Immediately on Red: pause traffic, execute rollback or mitigation per contingency lattice

Contingency lattice (quick guide):
- If latency p95 Red: reduce traffic by half, enable emergency autoscale, open scaling ticket, pause further ramp
- If error rate Red and correlated to model: switch to previous model variant, route new requests to fallback path
- If logging/observability degraded: abort ramp, capture disk snapshots, escalate to SRE and observability lead
- If cost overruns Red: cap burst capacity, enable cheaper quantized model variant, notify finance

Automated rollback rules (examples):
- Trigger rollback if any lane remains Red for > 15m and is impacting user sessions
- Soft rollback (reduce to last stable traffic %), hard rollback (full route to previous deploy) — runbook links below

Communication plan:
- Primary channel: #launch-commander (Slack) — commander posts one-line status each tick
- Pager: on-call SRE for infra; on-call Applied ML for model issues
- External comms: CS lead drafts proactive customer note if incident exceeds 30m

Post-launch (0–72h) monitoring and handoff:
- Run 24h regression sweep against canonical eval set (Applied ML)
- Finance reviews token cost delta at 24h and 72h
- Product ops to collect commander notes, timeline, and decisions for postmortem doc

Postmortem prompts (to capture in the final doc):
- What unexpected signals appeared and when?
- Which mitigations worked and which didn’t?
- Was the traffic cadence optimal? Where to tighten or loosen thresholds?
- Action items owner assignment + target completion dates

Open questions / items to resolve before final signoff:
- Do we have a synthetic probe to cover the new edge-case prompt series? (Assigned: Observability)
- Is the cheaper quantized variant validated for quality at 99% similarity on core intents? (Assigned: Applied ML)

Quick links and runbooks referenced:
- Rollback runbook: CONFLUENCE-12345
- Monitoring dashboards: https://grafana.redwood-inference/launch-dashboards
- Release PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/412
- Tickets: JIRA-PLAT-987 (routing policy), JIRA-ML-221 (model validation)

Notes to commander: keep updates terse; when in doubt mark Amber and call for a 5-minute focused triage. Capture timestamps for every change (this ledger becomes the single source of truth for the postmortem).

End of ledger (use this file to paste commander snapshots during the window).
